newsitem.title: USA: Petrobras says negotiating Iraqi price formula.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras says negotiating Iraqi price formula.

text.p: Brazil's state oil company Petrobras is negotiating a price formula with Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) to buy 20,000 to 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi crude, a Petrobras official said Wednesday.
"The volume we have in mind, if we can come to an agreement, is no more than 30,000 barrels per day," the official said.
Petrobras is looking to secure a slice of the $2 billion of oil Iraq is allowed to sell over the next six months under the terms of a humanitarian deal with the United Nations.
The Brazilian company is interested in buying either or both Basrah Light and Kirkuk crude from Iraq, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
"Petrobras and SOMO have to agree on a formula and SOMO has to submit it to the U.N. Discussions are going on," the official said.
Before Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, Petrobras bought a peak of 300,000 bpd of Basrah Light and Kirkuk on a term and spot basis.
Before 1990, Kirkuk for Brazil was priced off of benchmark Brent plus Alaska North Slope, while Basrah Light was priced off a combination of Oman and Dubai crudes, the official said.
He confirmed that Brazil now imports about 600,000 bpd of crude from countries such as West Africa, Colombia and Argentina.
He added that the Iraqi crude could possibly displace some West African barrels, although the West African grades that Petrobras buys are higher quality than Iraqi oil.
